page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r6a.2xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance running on a KVM hypervisor. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 7H12 processor clocked at 2.6 GHz, delivering 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 4 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The instance provides 64.0 GB of system memory, matching an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio. The CPU topology features 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 16 MB of L3 cache, with x86_64 instruction set support including AES, SHA-NI, AVX, and BMI2, while omitting AVX-512 extensions.

The hardware configuration does not bundle local ephemeral storage, requiring network-attached block storage volumes for persistent data. Dedicated network throughput is configured with a baseline bandwidth of 2 Gbps. The instance includes no GPU acceleration, focusing entirely on memory-heavy x86 compute workloads.

Benchmark results place the instance mostly in the middle tier for compute, memory, and application operations. On Geekbench 6, it scores 1301 in single-core and 4891 in multi-core testing, while recording a PassMark CPU score of 10308.35. While cached memory bandwidth performs well at 400.15 GB/sec on small 16 KB blocks, uncached operations drop to 30.8 GB/sec for reads and 15.87 GB/sec for writes. Extreme CPU stress benchmarks show lower-tier performance with stress-ng, reflecting the conservative base clock of the EPYC Rome platform compared to newer architectures.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the high RAM allocation per core makes this instance cost-effective for caching and in-memory architectures where raw clock speed is secondary to available memory capacity. It achieves 7.13 million operations per second on Redis SET workloads and 6.77 GB/sec throughput for static web serving. These characteristics make ecs.r6a.2xlarge suited for medium-scale in-memory databases, Redis caches, operational stores, and memory-bound enterprise backend applications.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r6a.2xlarge is a memory-optimized instance featuring 8 dedicated vCPUs from an AMD EPYC 7H12 processor at 2.6 GHz, paired with 64.0 GB of RAM. Designed for memory-intensive workloads, it provides an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio supported by 16 MB of L3 cache and a 2 Gbps network baseline. The instance does not include bundled local storage or GPU accelerators, relying on remote block storage. In benchmarks, the ecs.r6a.2xlarge demonstrates solid operational metrics, delivering 7.13 million operations per second in Redis SET evaluations and average multi-core results in Geekbench and PassMark, although uncached memory bandwidth and heavy synthetic stress performance remain modest. The platform offers efficient resource density for memory-bound deployments, making it well fitted for in-memory databases, distributed caching layers, and intermediate-scale operational database engines.
